expectations.text: Before publishing, the code polls GET /{container-id}?fields=status (with error_message) and only proceeds once the containers (at least the video) report FINISHED.
expectations.evidence: wait_until_finished() (L278-303) loops over every pending container with api('GET', cid, fields='status,error_message') and returns only when none is still waiting. It runs on all three item containers before the parent is created (L371), and again on the carousel parent before _publish() (L375). The test asserts that the last GET of the video container C3 comes before the parent POST, and that the sleeps were [3, 6] (video IN_PROGRESS twice, then FINISHED). One minor deviation: polling starts at 3 s and doubles to 60 s, which is more aggressive at first than the docs' 'once per minute, no more than 5 minutes'. expectations.text: The code handles a container in ERROR (surfacing error_message), EXPIRED, and a polling timeout without publishing.
expectations.evidence: L292-293: status ERROR, EXPIRED or PUBLISHED raises ContainerFailed(cid, status, error_message, label). L298-300: passing the deadline raises StillProcessing, which main() turns into exit code 75 plus a --resume-items/--resume-parent command. Both exceptions propagate before _publish() runs, and main() prints ContainerFailed to stderr ('發文失敗：...'). Tests: test_video_error_stops_before_carousel_and_publish (error_message 'INVALID_ASPEC_RATIO' surfaced, 0 threads_publish calls, no parent created); test_resume_after_24h_reports_expired (EXPIRED raises ContainerFailed with the 24-hour hint); test_slow_video_times_out_then_resume_reuses_containers (sleeps total 300 s, 0 publish calls). expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: Unexpired: ensureValidToken (threadsToken.ts:231-237) throws EXPIRED before any refresh when expiresAt <= now. >=24 h: isRefreshDue (253-258) returns false when age < 24h+10min (MIN_AGE_FOR_REFRESH_MS). Well before expiry: refresh when age >= 7 days (refreshAfterDays default 7) or <= 10 days left. Persisted with expiry: saveRefreshed (260-293) writes {accessToken, issuedAt: now, expiresAt: now + expires_in*1000 (fallback: debug_token expires_at), dataAccessExpiresAt, userId, updatedAt} via FileTokenStore.save (tmp file + fsync + rename, mode 0600). Independent grader simulation of 120 daily 09:00 runs with a mocked refresh endpoint: refreshes on days 5,12,19,...,117 (every 7 days), never refreshed a token younger than 24 h, minimum remaining validity 54 days, 0 alerts. Re-run executor tests 'expired -> EXPIRED, no refresh attempted', 'unknown expiry refreshes once >24h old, never before' and '8 days old -> refreshed, saved ... expiresAt = T0 + 5184000 s' all pass.

expectations.evidence: Partly met. MET: (1) A 24 h minimum-age gate applies when the issue time is known: MIN_TOKEN_AGE_FOR_REFRESH_MS = 24h + 5min, `if (obtained !== null && nowMs - obtained < MIN_TOKEN_AGE_FOR_REFRESH_MS) return false` (L37, L410). (2) Refresh fires when 30 days or less remain (refreshWhenRemainingDays default 30, L243/L415). (3) The new token is saved together with `expiresAt = now + expires_in` via fromTokenResponse + store.save (L421-423, L496-506). FileTokenStore writes the JSON atomically with mode 600. NOT MET, the 'only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old' clause: (a) There is no expiry check before calling refresh. shouldRefresh returns true whenever `expires - nowMs <= refreshWhenRemainingMs`, which includes tokens already past their expiry. Grader probe: a token whose stored expiresAt = now − 1 day triggers calls to /refresh_access_token and then /v1.0/me, and only then a critical alert and ThreadsTokenInvalidError. The executor's own test 'token 已失效' depends on this behaviour. (b) Tokens seeded from the environment or imported via the CLI have obtainedAt = null, so the 24 h guard is skipped and `if (expires === null) return true` refreshes them immediately. Grader probe: importToken() followed by getAccessToken() at the same instant makes 1 refresh call. The code knowingly does this: the NEW_IMPORT_GRACE_MS comment says these failures are 'mostly just not 24 h old yet' and suppresses the alert for 48 h. response.md tells the user to re-authorize by updating THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN and restarting ('以後重新授權：直接更新 THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN，再重啟服務就好'), so every re-authorization leads to a refresh attempt on a token that is almost certainly under 24 h old. The docs' /debug_token endpoint returns issued_at and expires_at and could have supplied the missing age, but the code never uses it. The steady-state path is sound and the practical harm is small (failed calls, retried the next day). Under a strict reading, though, the 'only refreshes…' gate is missing for expired tokens and for tokens of unknown age.

expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: Partly met. FAIL under the strict reading this eval's grader applied in iteration 1 to the same pattern. MET: (1) A 24 h minimum-age gate applies when the issue time is known: MIN_AGE_BEFORE_REFRESH_MS = DAY_MS and `if (token.issuedAt && now - Date.parse(token.issuedAt) < MIN_AGE_BEFORE_REFRESH_MS) return false` (token.ts L26, L283). Test '發出未滿 24 小時不續期' passes. (2) Refresh fires when 50 days or less remain (refreshWhenExpiresWithinDays default 50, L165/L286), about every 10 days, well before the 60-day expiry. (3) The new token is persisted with expiresAt = now + expires_in (toStoredToken L354-369, store.save L268) via FileTokenStore (tmp file + rename, mode 0600). Re-authorized tokens imported through the CLI are treated as freshly issued (importLongLivedToken sets issuedAt = now, L222-223), so they wait 24 h. This is better than the iteration-1 baseline. NOT MET, the 'only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old' clause: (a) There is no expiry check before calling refresh. shouldRefresh returns true whenever `Date.parse(token.expiresAt) - now <= this.refreshWithinMs`, which includes tokens already past expiry. Grader probe: a stored token with expiresAt = now - 1 day made calls to /refresh_access_token and then /v1.0/me, and only then threw ThreadsReauthRequiredError. The executor's own test '已過期無法續期' (test L216-226) depends on this, since it mocks the refresh endpoint to return 190. (b) The token bootstrapped from THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN is stored with issuedAt = null (L343), so the 24 h guard is skipped and `if (!token.expiresAt) return true` (L285) refreshes it immediately at unknown age. The probe showed 1 refresh call on the first getAccessToken(), and response.md says so ('第一次執行時會匯入，並馬上續期一次'). The docs' /debug_token (issued_at/expires_at) could have supplied the age but is not used. The steady-state path is sound and the practical harm is small: the failed calls are handled. Under the strict reading, though, the gate is missing for known-expired tokens and for the bootstrap token of unknown age.

expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: Step 2 refuses a token whose stored expiry has passed: it calls alert() and throws ReauthorizationRequiredError, and the mock run shows no refresh call. Step 3 refreshes only when the token is at least Math.max(refreshAfterDays, 1) days old (default 7). In the mock run a 12-hour-old token was not refreshed even with refreshAfterDays=0, and a 7-day-old token was. Refreshing at day 7 leaves about 53 days before the 60-day expiry. refresh() saves {accessToken, issuedAt, expiresAt = now + expires_in, falling back to 60 days} through TokenStore. FileTokenStore writes a temp file and renames it, with mode 600. The mock token file held NEW1 with expiresAt 2026-12-13T00:59:04Z (now + 5183944 s), and the next run used that saved token. Caveat: when the token's age is unknown (imported from env and debug_token refused), the code refreshes immediately, possibly on a token under 24 h old. expectations.text: Refresh logic follows the documented rules: only refreshes a token that is unexpired and at least 24 h old, refreshes well before the ~60-day expiry, and persists the new token together with its expiry.
expectations.evidence: Unexpired: assertNotExpired (tokenManager.ts L243-250) throws before any refresh when expiresAt <= now. Age: isRefreshDue (L203-207) requires now - issuedAt >= minAgeMs, default 24 h + 10 min (L103). Timing: it also requires remaining life <= 30 days (L101), so a 60-day token is renewed around day 30 with about 30 daily retries left. Persistence: refresh() builds { accessToken: res.access_token, issuedAt: attemptAt, expiresAt: issuedAt + expires_in*1000 } (L309-321) and calls store.save (L299). FileTokenStore writes the JSON atomically (tmp file + rename, mode 600). Tests cover each rule: 40 days left means no call; 20 days left means refresh, and the saved accessToken='NEW' with expiresAt=NOW+5184000s; a token under 24 h old is not refreshed even when expiry is unknown; a known-expired token throws without any API call. Caveat: a token whose issue time is unknown (bootstrapped from THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN or imported via the CLI) is treated as old enough. My probe showed one refresh call on the first run, with the rejection tolerated as a warning. Without debug_token the age cannot be known, so this is defensible, but in that state there is no strict 24 h gate.

expectations.text: Yesterday's posts are listed via GET /me/threads (or /{user-id}/threads) using since/until or timestamp filtering, with cursor pagination via paging.cursors.after and limit <= 100.
expectations.evidence: insights.ts L343-401 calls GET `${userId}/threads` (user id from /me) with fields id,media_type,permalink,text,timestamp, since=start-3600, until=end+3600 and limit=25 (PAGE_LIMIT). It then keeps posts whose timestamp is in [start, end) of the Taipei day. Pagination: it follows paging.next if present; otherwise it reads `body.paging?.cursors?.after` and re-requests with { ...baseParams, after }. It stops when there is no cursor, a repeated cursor, a short page or 20 pages. The official docs (Retrieve and Discover Posts.md) say the response 'will not include previous or next fields', so production would take the cursors.after branch. The executor's tests only exercise paging.next, so I ran a probe with doc-shaped responses (cursors only, 60 posts). The requests went after=null→C25→C50 with limit=25 and since/until on every page, and 60/60 posts were collected. Minor caveat: the docs require until <= now. The +1 h padding is fine for a 09:00 run but would break between 00:00 and 01:00 or when backfilling today.

If it returns success:true without hiding anything, the script logs action=hidden '已直接隱藏這則巢狀回覆', marks the reply handled and never checks again. Final skill version: 29/29 checks (100%) vs 25/29 without the skill (85% averaged per eval). Every eval scores at least as well with the skill.

Baseline variance is real: eval 2 without the skill passed 9/9 this round after failing pagination and refresh checks in rounds 1 and 2. With one run per configuration, a single lucky or unlucky run moves the averages a lot.

Remaining baseline misses are knowledge gaps: it still hedges on ghost post + poll and ships a mode that tries the forbidden combination, shows no exact payloads in the reply, omits the 100-follower requirement for profile_lookup, and calls manage_reply on nested replies before falling back.

Graders found a few overstatements in with-skill replies that trace to the skill's wording: a ghost post's link preview restriction presented as stated in the docs (the docs only say text spoilers are the sole supported feature), 'will definitely be rejected' where the docs don't say how the API reacts, and the two profile-discovery endpoints' 1,000-request limits treated as one shared quota.
Speed and cost: with the skill, mean ~706 s vs ~963 s and ~178K vs ~189K tokens.
